#3767. GTA 6 day-one sales are enormous, estimates suggest, making previous $2 billion opening weekend predictions seem conservative

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking company Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

#3765. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 breaks the game into star system mini-campaigns, each with their own stories and objectives

"We want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy."

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do."

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that."

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

2026 has been pretty weird, but I wasn't expecting a dino sighting.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I thought we'd already gotten our fill of prehistoric creatures on the 2026 movie schedule, thanks to The End of Oak Street. The film sees Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor spending a summer trying to survive a neighborhood full of creatures that should have been extinct for millions of years. Then, as soon as the movie hit streaming, the internet started arguing over footage supposedly showing a pterodactyl flying over Mexico. The timing feels a little too perfect.

The latest monster-of-the-week discussion took off on November 13, when someone posted images to Reddit's r/Cryptozoology forum. The poster claimed the winged creature had been caught on airport security footage in Ciudad Juárez and that additional witnesses had photographs. None of that was verified, but you can probably guess how the comments went.

I'll give the image this much: It's pretty cool. The creature has an enormous wingspan, a long, pointed head, and a silhouette you'd expect to see flying over the Platt family's house in The End of Oak Street. Of course, it also looks suspiciously like something you'd find in Jurassic Park. Several Reddit users noticed that resemblance, too, and weren't particularly convinced.

There's apparently more to the sighting. According to Mexican outlet El Financier, an earlier video, reportedly recorded October 29 in the Anapra area of Ciudad Juárez, shows a mysterious winged figure flying across the night sky. Jaime Maussan, a Mexican broadcaster known for his interest in UFOs and other unexplained phenomena, picked up the footage and helped spread the story. Before long, additional alleged sightings circulated online, and naturally, the internet had a field day.

No cryptic sighting is worth its weight in dino dung unless the internet loses its collective mind, and the comments weren't disappointing. One commenter with the username r/alfred0t0rnad0 pretty much summed up my feelings:

Somebody else was considerably more enthusiastic about the possibility of prehistoric creatures making a comeback. R/AsadAliShadowhunter wrote:

At this point, I hope the Dinos are back.

Look, I'm not opposed to a little prehistoric excitement. I'd just prefer anything with a 20-foot wingspan to stay away from my backyard.

Those two comments barely scratch the surface, though. Some users had legitimate questions about the footage, while others were just enjoying the absurdity. Here are a few of my favorites:

Personally, I'm partial to the idea of a prehistoric creature emerging from the hollow Earth for tacos. But the commenters questioning how an entire population of giant flying reptiles could have gone unnoticed for millions of years have a pretty good point.

The End Of Oak Street Ending: Yes, They Had Conversations About The Dog Dying

There's also the small matter of what local authorities have said about the footage. EFE's fact-checking team reported Wednesday that Ciudad Juárez's civil protection director, Sergio Rodríguez, dismissed the recordings as digital entertainment content. One widely shared version also appears to show signs of AI manipulation, although the origins of the various clips haven't all been established.

Unfortunately for those of us hoping The End of Oak Street had somehow become a documentary, there's no credible evidence that a pterodactyl is flying around Mexico. Still, I have to admit I've enjoyed watching the internet speculate over the possibility.

The End of Oak Street is now streaming with an HBO Max subscription, which makes it an excellent choice if this whole thing has you craving some cinematic dinosaurs.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3763. GTA 6 Has A Surprising Late Game Cameo That Knocked Me On My Ass

Across social media and YouTube, a massive spoiler from the final chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6 has been spreading online. It is a cameo by a past character that has people going wild. Some fans who have sped through the game’s story are rushing to be the first to share it online. Others don’t believe it’s even real. I’m here to confirm that, yes, the wild cameo you saw is real, and it made me scream.

This is your last warning. The next paragraphs are going to completely reveal the spoiler. If you are a massive GTA nerd and/or love surprises, stop reading now and close this article. Seriously, you’ll thank me later. For those who don’t care about spoilers, GTA lore, or who were never planning to play the game, let’s dive into one of the biggest surprises hidden within the massive world of GTA 6. Last chance to turn away. See you on the other side.

Near the tail end of GTA 6‘s big, epic crime story, Jason and Lucia begin working with Giorgio, a wealthy shipping magnate. He’s been working with some cartels and Eastern European criminals and has been letting them use his ships to smuggle cocaine across the ocean. It’s been working out pretty well for a while, but by the time Jason and Lucia show up, the Coast Guard has seized all the drugs from a recent shipment. He has a plan to rob the Coast Guard, get his coke back, and make everyone happy before they come to his big penthouse and kill him. But then, just as his big heist is coming together, a higher-up from the Balkan criminal family he’s been working with shows up to put a bullet in his brain.

And the person sent to Vice City is none other than Grand Theft Auto IV protagonist Niko Bellic. Yup. As shared online by many players already, a much older Niko shows up in two cutscenes to threaten Giorgio and then to collect the drugs once the heist works out. Here are those cutscenes:

I will admit that before he showed up, when I heard Giorgio yell out, “Daddy’s back bitches!” I chuckled to myself and thought, “Oh nice, a reference to the opening line of GTA IV. Cute.” I had no idea that would be followed up by the reveal of fucking Niko Bellic. I might have let out a scream and paused the game in pure shock and amazement.

We’ve not heard much about Niko since the ending of GTA IV. So seeing him back in the flesh, with grey hair, was great. And I love that Rockstar got back the original voice actor, Michael Hollick. And yes, that’s why in the credits of GTA 6 posted online by Rockstar, he is simply labeled “The Hitman.”

I can’t wait for more GTA fans and nerds to discover this moment and share their reactions. I’ll have more to share about the cameo and how it came about soon from my interview with Rockstar Games head of production Rob Nelson. But for now, let’s just enjoy the fact that Niko is back, baby.

#3762. Jennifer Lawrence Reveals Her New ‘Full C’ Breast Implants on ‘WWHL’

Jennifer Lawrence is getting candid about going under the knife.

The actress, 36, confirmed she had gotten a boob job while appearing on the Thursday, November 19, episode of Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen alongside her Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping costar, Josh Hutcherson.

The admission came as she was giving her “hot takes” on Bravo celebrities. At one point host Andy Cohen, 58, asked Lawrence, “Is it a mystery to you how a boob could break Hailey Glassman’s nose?”

In response, the Oscar winner said, “Yes, and I have implants.” Drawing attention to her bust, she added, “Yeah, they’re new.”

Cohen complimented Lawrence, calling the implants “beautiful” and questioned her about the size she opted for.  “What is that? Are those Bs?” Cohen asked.

“No, it’s a full C. I think?” Lawrence said. “It’s the same size that they were.”

The Don’t Look Up star went on to joke, “Anyway, I’ve broken two noses.”

Lawrence has previously been an open book about her cosmetic surgery procedures.

Speaking to Vogue for an article published on September 3, Lawrence revealed all the cosmetic work she’s had done.

“I need to have movement in my face — I get baby Botox, but I can’t do a lot,” she shared. “If my skin is going to be a little saggier than I would like, at least it looks dewy and pretty.”

Lawrence noted she was also considering fat transfer, which can help restore volume and smooth wrinkles but was yet to take the plunge.

“I’m really nervous about these fat transfers,” Lawrence admitted to the magazine. “I support other people doing them because I want to continue to watch and see what happens, but I don’t know about that.”

“I mean, I would love to have a buccal fat removal,” the No Hard Feelings star added of the procedure that takes out fat pads from the cheeks to create a more sculpted face. “I can’t because everybody would know, but just know that I want that.” Lawrence also opened up about other beauty treatments that she doesn’t necessarily enjoy getting done.

Last month, Lawrence shared her desire to look like a “sexy mom” after welcoming two sons, with her husband Cooke Maroney.

“I want to be a sexy mom,” she told The Cut in October. “At drop-off, I want to look like a woman that has her s*** together even when I’ve just woken up and don’t have my s*** together.”

The console release of GTA 6 is here, in case you hadn't noticed. And us PC gamers are desperate to get hold of a version of our own, particularly as modders say it'll be playable on god's own platform within a week. Be careful what you click on, though, as NordVPN's threat intelligence team has discovered a nasty-sounding scam package on the dark web.

The company has posted a warning on X of a "GTA 6 PC scam kit" doing the rounds on the more dubious parts of the internet, using a fake GTA 6 PC port as bait.

A “GTA 6 PC scam kit” — yours for just $200. That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner. The bait? A fake “GTA 6 PC Port.” But GTA 6 is console-only — there's no PC version coming on launch day. If you see one, it’s a scam. If it doesn’t come from the creators, don't click it!November 19, 2026

The package is said to be for sale for $200, or twice what a single copy of Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition costs at retail. Included is a crypto wallet drainer, a fake "GTA6 Keygen.exe," and a hidden crypto miner. There's also a YouTube Shorts bot within the package, designed to help it spread.

All of which sounds comprehensively designed to screw over PC gamers looking to get their hands on GTA 6 ahead of an official release.

Speaking to Tech Radar ahead of the games launch, NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis said: "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore."

"People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," says Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam."

NordVPN isn't the only security provider warning of GTA 6 scams. Malwarebytes has detailed a number of dodgy sites that supposedly offer access to the game, each using the hype as a lure to convince you to give away your details and funnel you into various schemes.

All of which compels me to restate the facts: GTA 6 does not have a PC release at the time of writing. In fact, it's not even been announced by Rockstar at this point. The game is available in Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 versions only, and while modders seem to be beavering away on an unofficial PC version based on a leaked Xbox build, it's not available yet.

Don't let yourself be fooled into clicking shady links—and if you don't have a console like my good self, be prepared to wait. May I suggest playing all the other excellent games in your Steam backlog instead? It's not like we're short of PC games in general, you know.

#3760. UK Prime Minister won't be playing GTA 6, government says, while hailing Rockstar Games a "British success story"

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it."

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else."

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Among the book-to-screen adaptations I'm most excited for in 2027 is The Nightingale. Based on Kristin Hannah's brilliant novel, the story follows two sisters in France whose lives go in different directions during World War II, and the choices they have to make along the way.

Directed by Michael Morris and starring real-life sisters Dakota and Elle Fanning, The Nightingale follows their characters' stories as they find themselves getting more involved in what's going around them as the Nazis invade France. While Hannah's novel is historical fiction, the book is inspired by true accounts of the war.

The more I've learned about World War II, particularly in looking at the impact it had on different regions of the world, the more interested I've become in hearing stories about the involvement of women in the war. Naturally, I was drawn to Hannah's novel. (She also wrote an amazing historical fiction novel called The Women, which is set during the Vietnam War that I highly recommend.) Exciting, emotional and powerful, The Nightingale absolutely lived up to the hype (4.6+ out of 5 on Goodreads with over 2 million ratings?!), and I can't wait to see the movie.

In The Nightingale, Vianne (Dakota Fanning) is trying to keep her daughter safe as the Nazis begin to occupy France. Meanwhile, her younger sister, Isabelle (Elle Fanning), wants to take a more active role in what's going on, and finds herself joining the resistance. While both sisters take a very different approach to survival during this turbulent and dangerous time, the story really shows the way courage can emerge in different ways.

With just a minute's worth of footage, this new teaser gives us a good look at what these two sisters face as their entire world is upended by this war. Vianne is determined to keep her family safe, while Isabelle -- despite her very young age -- can't stand by and not try to help make a difference. In the end, both women end up finding themselves faced with dangerous situations and impossible choices that require quick thinking and more courage than most could muster when push comes to shove. Whether they're protecting children and innocents or going undercover to help with the resistance, the story of these sisters shows the impact one woman can make amidst the chaos of war.

Of course, the teaser leaves off with "She'll need a codename," which points directly to the title of the movie.

I'm excited about everything to do with this adaptation, from the source material, to the stars, to what we're seeing here. While many World War II movies emphasize the invasions and battles, stories like The Nightingale -- whether fiction, non-fiction, or inspired by true events -- remind us of the impact of war on the spaces in between the battles, and the civilians who find (sometimes crucial) ways to help.

The Nightingale is set to hit theaters on the 2027 movie schedule on March 19, 2027.

#3758. GTA 6 Release Was So Big It Broke Internet Download Records Twice In One Week

Without a physical release, the millions of people jumping into Grand Theft Auto VI have had no choice but to download the game. And at over 200 GB per person, that’s been no small deal. The sheer demand and strain on digital networks has led to the record for internet usage globally being broken. Not once, but twice.

The figures were reported by DE-CIX, an internet infrastructure company, based on data going through its networks. At their peak on the evening before the gameâs official release date, downloads surpassed 33.03 terabits per second, which the company calculates as enough to download 13 copies of the game per second. This appears to be record traffic. The previous record was set just one week prior, and that was again because of GTA 6, when downloads for the game first began on November 10. Additional regional records were broken across the U.S. in areas like Phoenix, Chicago and Dallas.

And this is just one exchange, so itâs likely the numbers across all exchanges are much higher. It seems to be a record-breaking release across the board, with other internet service providers around the world reporting similarly unprecedented traffic.

There are still no official figures for the gameâs sales, but many analysts expect the game to make over $3 billion in its opening weekend, and potentially surpass over 20 million copies sold before it even hit the market. Numbers were already at an estimated eight million copies before downloads began at the start of November.

#3755. Rob Lowe Claps Back at Criticism of His Choice to Work With Ben Shapiro

Rob Lowe is standing by his decision to work with Ben Shapiro — despite attracting some backlash for his call.

Speaking on the “Second Thought” podcast this week, Lowe, 62, defended starring in Confession, a psychological historical drama written by Shapiro, who is known for his right-wing political views.

Lowe insisted that he took on the project because he was more interested in the script than the politics surrounding its writer.

“It’s a really, really, really interesting assessment of not only where our world is, but where Hollywood is as well,” Lowe said on the podcast. “So, I read the script. It was written by Ben Shapiro. I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic.’”

Lowe said Shapiro initially asked whether he knew a leading man in his 50s who wouldn’t be intimidated by the idea of working with him. Lowe was quick to volunteer himself.

“And I go, ‘Yeah, me,’” Lowe recalled telling Shapiro, adding that he was comfortable taking on the role.

Lowe continued, “And he goes, ‘You’re good with it?’ I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’”

Confession, which is directed by Václav Marhoul, follows the interrogation of a prisoner in a Stalin-era Russian jail. The film also stars Nick Nolte, James Franco and Emile Hirsch.

The film premiered at the Warsaw Film Festival in October, then received a one-night-only theatrical release on November 11. Confession then dropped on The Daily Wire’s streaming platform the same day.

During his podcast appearance, Lowe also expressed frustration that the movie failed to secure a wider festival run.

“And so, we make the movie, and the movie is what it is. It’s a movie,” he said. “Look, it is challenging. It is a tough watch, but I see the movies that are celebrated out there. I see the movies that are picked — we got turned down by every single film festival, summarily frog marched out of any conversation.”

Lowe went on to suggest that political considerations were behind the film’s rejection, saying, “I see what they’re picking up, and it’s all political, right?”

He added, “The thought would be we’d play in a film festival, we would get some buzz — never happened. And then you know, Netflix would pick it up or this one would pick. Crickets. Absolute crickets.”

After the film struggled to find a home, Lowe explained that he was happy that Daily Wire eventually became Confession’s distributor.

“I’m like, ‘Hell yeah!’” Lowe said. “I want people to see this movie. And good for them for putting it out.”

#3753. Don’t Expect To See Vice City For A Long Time In GTA 6

For those still waiting for GTA 6 to unlock, it's possible you have something of a mistaken impression of what the early hours will look like. Despite partially sharing a setting with GTA Vice City, you should not expect to be walking up the game's equivalent of Ocean Drive and Miami Beach in the opening minutes, as in the 2002 game. Far from it.

As we noted in our video discussion on why we gave GTA 6 a 10/10 in our review, Tamoor and Jake did some expectation-setting. Rather than starting the game in Vice City, you'll instead spend the opening hours in a smaller corner of the state of Leonida, Key Lento. Vice City is undoubtedly the crown jewel of the game's world, but it could be as much as 20 hours before you reach it, depending on how you play.

This seems to be a deliberate decision that, as Tam says, allows you to progress through the world at roughly the same pace as the ambitions of co-stars Lucia and Jason. The opening area may not be as glamorous as Vice City, but it is no less detailed than the rest of the game. It's possible it's only meant to last you around 5-6 hours, but we found it easy to get lost spending far more time than that, which resulted in Tam not reaching Vice City until after 15 or 16 hours.

Key Lento provides a good look at how the game and its simulation work, letting you eventually progress to a much larger space (seriously, the map is huge) with a good understanding of how things work.

All of this is to say, the glitz and glamor of Vice City are waiting for you--eventually. To make the most of the opening hours, be sure to check out our guide on what to do in GTA 6 first.

#3752. Bigfoot Is Back In GTA 6, And Apparently He Smells Revolting

Grand Theft Auto games have been home to some weird phenomena over the years, and in GTA 6, it looks like Bigfoot is back and stinkier than ever. As the game steadily rolls out worldwide--or as people digitally immigrate to New Zealand for early access--streamers have been posting clips online of their encounters with the cryptid, and this time, it doesn't look like a man in a suit.

It looks like the Bigfoot sighting is tied to a mission in GTA 6, as the mysterious creature is wandering the woods of Leonida and it takes off in a panic when you encounter it. Another clip shows a strange encounter in the woods, with the player interacting with an effigy that emits noxious fumes and knocks them out. In a brief cutscene, Bigfoots, uh, really big feet, can be seen approaching Jason as he drifts in and out of consciousness.

In that first clip, Bigfoot is also covered in a cloud of fumes, which likely references stories about the mythical creature's potent stench. For GTA--and Red Dead Redemption--fans, this isn't the first time that they've been involved in a Bigfoot sighting, as encounters with it stretch back decades.

Back in 2004, rumors began to circulate about Bigfoot existing in GTA: San Andreas, but Rockstar dismissed these reports as false in 2005. A few years later, in Red Dead Redemption's Undead Nightmare expansion, protagonist John Marston was tasked with hunting down a pack of Sasquatches, and it was eventually revealed that the creatures were peaceful, capable of human speech, and now going extinct thanks to a certain trigger-happy cowboy.

Bigfoot would appear in GTA 5, as getting 100% completion in the game would unlock a new mission where co-protagonist Franklin hunts down a creature in Blaine Woods, only to discover it was a man in a costume. As an extra joke, the Bigfoot impersonator drops a few references to Red Dead Redemption's infamous encounter, but that doesn't mean the real Bigfoot isn't lurking in GTA 5. You could use the thermal scope on the sniper rifle supplied to you to spot a bipedal creature watching you during the "Predator" mission, and eating a golden Peyote plant under specific environmental conditions would turn players into Bigfoot.

Red Dead Redemption 2 brought an air of mystery back to the Bigfoot mythos, as you could find a gigantic skeleton half-buried in the snow high up on Mount Shann, and protagonist Arthur Morgan could also speak to an unseen figure that was heavily implied to be Bigfoot.

#3751. The Obvious Problem With Survivor’s Coin Flip Isn’t Even My Biggest Problem With It

Let's talk about why the coin flip doesn't work.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There’s a really obvious problem with Survivor’s Coin Flip. The new game mechanic that was introduced last season gives one player a chance to double the prize pot and earn themselves an idol if they call a coin flip correctly or sends them home immediately if they don't. In theory, it's a high stakes game of chance that should make for exciting television, but there's an inherent structural issue that doesn't play well with network television.

The episode runtime spoiled the result of last night’s coin flip, just as it spoiled the result of Rick Devens’ coin flip on 50, just as it will likely spoil the results of any coin flip the show does in the future. Every episode ends with someone going home; so, if there’s a few minutes left when the person flips the coin, it’s bad news for them. If there’s enough time to do an entire vote after they flip the coin, it’s good news for them.

It’s an obvious problem and one that’s very valid for fans to complain about, but it’s actually not my biggest problem with the coin flip twist. I want it gone because it creates the potential to send someone home without being voted out.

Yes, sometimes people go home because they quit or get medically evacuated (get better soon, New England Rob), but that’s a natural byproduct of trying to survive in harsh conditions, not a production decision to try and generate drama. Yes, when there are four players left, we get a fire-making competition instead of a traditional vote, but that at least feels on brand to the show and also, is the subject of fan protests every single season. This coin flip thing, however, feels entirely different. It feels like a wacky gameshow element producers inserted because wouldn’t that make for fun television?

As a Survivor fan, however, I don’t think it makes for fun television. I am watching the show because I want to see the castaways actually play the social strategic game they signed up for. I want to see them try to navigate the island and their competitors and figure out how to survive each tribal council using the tools at their disposal. I don’t want to see one of them do an entirely luck-based challenge to decide their fate. That’s not the point of the game.

To be clear, luck does play a huge role on Survivor. Castaways go home all the time because they’re swapped onto the wrong tribe or their team loses an immunity challenge because other people blow a huge lead on a puzzle or whatever. The game is rarely fair, but in theory, even when it’s unfair, the player still has a chance to wiggle out of whatever danger they’re in. Get swapped onto a tribe against four members of an alliance? Try to find a crack and pit them against each other. Figure out that you’re on the wrong side of the numbers a few hours before tribal council? Go hunt for idols or make a fake idol or do something reckless to try and blow up someone else’s spot.

Those desperate shenanigans usually don’t work, but it still feels like the losing player’s fate was in their own hands. Maybe if they had found the right combination of words. Maybe if they had hunted in a different location. Maybe if they had built better relationships with the other side earlier in the game. Maybe if they had done something else, things would have been different.

You could look at the coin flip and say that’s an example of Survivor giving a player on the bottom a mechanism to change their fate, but to me, flipping a coin just feels so luck-based. It’s like a more obnoxious version of the Shot In The Dark, but at least with the Shot In The Dark, every player is given the same token and can use it in creative ways to build trust, try to avoid using an idol, etc. With the coin flip, it feels like a once a season game of chance for one player to do as part of a special event episode.

I didn’t like the coin flip when Rick Devens did it during 50. I didn’t like it last night when Lewis Kelly did it during 51, and I’m not going to like it next season when some unknown person flips it during 52. Yes, the runtime is an issue, but the bigger problem is it doesn’t feel authentic to the spirit of Survivor and the game they’re playing.

This season has been so good thus far. The characters are fantastic. The gameplay is chaotic. It's a great time, which is why I just want to see everyone play the actual show I signed up to watch.

#3749. GTA 6 Owner Take-Two’s Stock Adds Billions After Rave Reviews, But It’s Not All Good News

After more than 10 years of waiting, Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally available now (at least in New Zealand and Australia). The anticipation has been sky-high for both consumers and investors alike, and Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, is seeing a huge uplift in its share price today after the game's overwhelmingly positive reviews landed.

Take-Two shares rose by nearly7% in pre-market trading today, and moved higher from there as the day went on. This meant that Take-Two's market cap grew by billions today alone.

Stock analysts expected share value to increase in the lead-up to launch, and many expect it to go higher still due to the expected launches of GTA Online and a PC edition of the game in 2027.

While Take-Two's stock price is popping today, Take-Two remains down close to 20% so far in 2026 and is down about 15% over the past 12 months. Why? No one really knows, because the stock market is fickle. Take-Two's stock price got hammered earlier this year when Google announced new AI software to make games, presumably spooking investors. The stock has not recovered since.

The 52-week high for Take-Two is $265.65, and the 52-week low is $183.86.

Zooming further out, though, Take-Two has been a fantastic investment for people who bought and held for a long time. As Rand Group points out, $10,000 invested into Take-Two when GTA 5 launched in 2013 has grown to more than $120,000 today.

GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. "GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," reviewer Tamoor Hussain said.

GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever.

#3748. Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond

It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the role of MI6 agent James Bond.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

Pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon. However, in February 2025, Broccoli and Wilson announced that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a new era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Although a new era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: They needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had announced that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007-sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

Technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don’t tell him that. During Vanity Fair’s lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z,” he said to Lawrence. “I am.” Hey, you’re only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “likes taking jobs of younger actors,” which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

Almost every leading man in Hollywood’s name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson’s take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve’s The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman’s studio, DC—last week, it was announced that the co-CEOs of DC Productions, James Gunn and Peter Safran, were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson’s schedule for some sexy espionage.

Still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashana Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person to ever to hold the 007 moniker, in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported in 2024 that Aaron Taylor-Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role, but those reports were never confirmed.

Although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn’t screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakistani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to, Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson, and, apparently, Harry Styles. At the end of the day, five actors reportedly screen-tested for the role: Slow Horse’s Jack Lowden, One Night Only’s Callum Turner, Disclosure Day’s Josh O’Connor, Superman’s Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last names to emerge as contenders for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a three-picture deal rather than a four-picture deal despite commanding a much higher salary than the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

It also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box-office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a reported budget of about $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner that earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there’s Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim drama starring Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way, Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit big with $62 million globally on an $14.5 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading-actor buzz. On top of it all, he’s still got Dune: Part Three with Denis Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

Ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, including producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve’s highly-anticipated Dune: Part Three, it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” said Villeneuve in a statement. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first-ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in six Bond films, including From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

After Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s GoldenEye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Will Pattison’s Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery’s throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy Who Shagged Me? In any case, let’s hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He’s going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

#3746. How Xbox’s Streaming Deal For GTA 6 Could Expand Its Marketshare By 30%

Microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92.

This is according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which said the streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%.

For anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA 6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, or even an Xbox One.

There are some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry said the Xbox Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that might not be an issue for everyone.

No such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5.

Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all.

Beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of users streaming a brand-new game like GTA 6 compared to Sony." 

"The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. "While PS5 users can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience."

Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 users ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more important to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said.

Under $100 to play GTA 6 on Xbox

Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen.

Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game.

This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere said, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used."

As announced previously, people can stream GTA 6 to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a Game Pass membership. The pricing is below.

Cloud playtime packs pricing:

  • 10 hours for $4
  • 25 hours for $8
  • 50 hours for $12

Coinciding with GTA 6's release and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are:

  • Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours
  • Game Pass Premium: 10 hours
  • Game Pass Essential: 5 hours

Even beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6 considering that a new Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for the cheapest new PS5.

GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

#3742. Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her

On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.

Despite its bladder-bothering length, The Odyssey stands as one of the year's most successful and thrilling movie experiences, and with the film now available to watch at your leisure, it's the perfect time to embark on the journey.

The Odyssey hit theaters back in July of this year, with a special encore run set for December. The home video release, on both physical disc and PVOD was Tuesday, November 17.

The home release of The Odyssey comes with a wealth of behind the scenes materials for film fans to sink their teeth into with Universal teasing: "Personally overseen by Christopher Nolan, this collection of 12 in-depth special features takes audiences inside every aspect of The Odyssey's ambitious production through exclusive behind-the-scenes footage and interviews with Nolan alongside key cast and crew who brought the epic to life. Together, these pieces showcase the artistry, innovation, and craftsmanship behind the landmark adaptation of Homer’s legendary tale."

Joe is a Journalist and Junior Editor based in the UK. He holds an undergrad in Film Studies and an MA in Journalism. His work has appeared in multiple national publications, such as The i Paper and The Telegraph. Joe's expertise cover TV and streaming. When he's not writing about TV, he's watching it. He also enjoys spending his free time reading, watching sports or catching live gigs

#3739. GTA 6’s Best Song Is A Nelly Furtado Cover From Azerbaijan

One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones. As a music-discovery vehicle, GTA: Vice City introduced me to many '80s classics across a variety of genres. With GTA 6 taking players to Leonida, in which Vice City is located, it's apt that the game features music that many probably would never hear anywhere else.

One of the radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM. It features covers of very-well-known songs that are performed by artists from around the world. It's a fantastic hook for a radio station and delivers some of the catchiest and most-unexpected covers from artists that have a pretty low profile outside of their home countries.

The first song I heard on the station, and the one that remains my absolute favorite, is a cover of Nelly Furtado's "Say It Right" from Azerbaijani artists Alim Qasimov and Farghana Qasimova. The duo are known for performing Mugham, a type of music that blends poetry, melody, and improvisation. I had never heard of them before playing GTA 6, but the music instantly transported me to my youth listening to Qawwali, a type of music that is rooted in Islamic sufism. 

Initially, my exposure to Qawwali, a type of music that is over 600 years old, was limited to my own home, but it has since gained a worldwide following thanks to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, who is known as the King of Kings of Qawwali. These days it's pretty common to hear songs that either sample or are inspired by Qawwali, but, even so, hearing Mugham in GTA 6 was a huge surprise. I didn't expect to be playing Rockstar's latest opus and be reminded of Qawwali.

I already love "Say It Right"--I think it's one of Furtado and producers Timbaland and Danja's best--but this cover draws out the melancholic soul that underpins the original, giving it a more emotional weight. Much of that can be attributed to the religious mysticism that both Mugham and Qawwali evoke. 

What I appreciate about this cover is how brilliantly it allows the unfamiliar to grasp what makes Mugham and Qawwali so beautiful by presenting it through a song that many people already have some familiarity with. Both types of music are performed by an ensemble, but the improvisational nature means that others are encouraged to contribute. The use of the kamancheh, tar, and daf, along with the vocals covering Furtado's chorus and the khananda's additions, come together to make the cover feel magical. 

There are other songs that will no doubt catch you by surprise on Kaleidoscope FM--another favourite is a South Asian cover of "Careless Whisper." Naturally, I was intrigued by how this station came to be and, according to Ivan Pavlovich, Rockstar's vice president of music, it stems from an obsession that studio co-founder Sam Houser has.

“Historically, we have always loved to champion a quirky, concept-driven station," Pavlovich told GameSpot. "Sam loves foreign-language covers of his favorite songs and thought this could be that station for GTA VI. Tracking down rights holders proved particularly tricky in certain countries."

The biggest surprise, however, is the radio station's host: Academy Award winner Jeremy Irons.

"Jeremy Irons has the perfect voice as the travel-weathered host telling tall tales of his adventures from around the world," Pavlovich added. "Jeremy loved the script, and nailed the wry humor of his character in one session. Hopefully, this station makes fans smile as much as we did when we were making it."

Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are available now. GameSpot gave it a 10/10, saying that it sets the standard for open worlds impossibly high.

In recent days, my inbox and, I’m sure, the inboxes of many a staffer at gaming publications have been flooded with emails from brands trying to capitalize in some way on all the GTA 6 hype. And look, I get it; of course marketers are going to see an opportunity in associating their brands with a pop culture event of this magnitude. Some are calling the release of GTA 6 the return of the monoculture, or maybe its last gasp. And some of what’s happening I think is fine. Zack caught a Panda Express ad earlier today on another site that was clearly designed to create an association in viewers’ minds between the game and the restaurant, even though there is no official collaboration between Rockstar and Panda Express.

I can’t be mad at this. I’ve been seeing this sort of thing my whole life, brands gesturing toward whatever the cultural vibe or flavor of the month is. It’s whatever, it’s fine. But some of the other efforts strike me as a bit more desperate, and a bit more clueless.

Case in point: Today I got an email announcing that Heinz, the ketchup brand, “Drops Real-Life GORGE Ketchup from Vice City.” Apparently inÂ GTA 6, you can see condiments that are styled to look like Heinz products, but the in-game brand is called Gorge. And sure, ifÂ GTAÂ is gonna spoof your product, I think turnabout is fair play and releasing your own real-life version of said product is fine from, like, an ethical standpoint. But it also strikes me as silly.

I think maybe for me the real problem with this effort had to do with some of the text in the associated email, which just made it all feel to me like an effort cooked up by boardroom marketing execs who don’t really know much about GTAÂ at all. For instance, one line in the email read, “Consider it the ultimate loot drop for ketchup-loving gamers.” Ah yes, if there’s one thing the gamers in my life love as much as spending some quality time in GTA, it’s KETCHUP! And also, GTAÂ doesn’t HAVE loot drops! I mean, maybe it should. Maybe the big climactic missions at the end of each chapter should have bosses you kill who have a 2.5-percent chance of dropping a Legendary pistol that does extra damage and freezes enemies in place with ice magic. But it doesn’t.

Anyway, if you want a shot at scoring some real-life Gorge Ketchup (and I know you do!), I guess visit this post on the Heinz Instagram for details. Happy Gorging!

TheÂ GTAÂ games are often story-generating machines. Part of the fun of playing them is getting to talk to your friends later about the wild encounters and experiences you had in-game. An anecdote about one such encounter from Jason Schreier’s review forÂ BloombergÂ seems to be persuading at least a few folks who previously weren’t interested in playing the game into potentially giving it a try.

It definitely makes for an attention-grabbing opener to the review. The anecdote reads:

Several hours into Grand Theft Auto VI, I watched a sedan get smashed from behind by a truck. I had been driving around Vice City, a fictionalized re-creation of Miami with such lifelike graphical fidelity that it can be hard to distinguish the video game from real-life footage, and I pulled to a stop when I saw the two vehicles collide. The truck driver scampered off, leaving the victim trapped in his seat as his engine began to catch fire. I ran over and helped him out of the car. He thanked me, reflecting in astonishment that heâd almost died. Then he noticed that the culprit was a delivery truck for Sahara, the Grand Theft Auto parody of Amazon. This was his big break, he declared. He could sue Sahara for millions.

But he needed demonstrable damages. So he took a deep breath, got back in the car, set his own legs on fire and then re-emerged with burns all over his body. He called his lawyer. Then, as an ambulance approached, he turned and asked me to be a witness in exchange for some of his inevitable payout. I thought about pressing a button to blackmail him but ultimately agreed to help, and he sent me a few thousand dollars on BuckMe, the gameâs version of Venmo.

This is the kind of encounter that Rockstar excels at, an event you just stumble upon that seems random but is actually crafted specifically to give the world that feeling of life, randomness, and spontaneity. And I’m sure this is just one of many such events you might come across in your time with the game.

It was enough to intrigue journalist and OnionÂ CEO Ben Collins, who posted the anecdote to Bluesky and said, “Had basically zero interest in playing GTA VI until I saw this lede in a Bloomberg review. It’s persuasive writing, at the very least.” Meanwhile,Â New York TimesÂ opinion columnist Jamelle Bouie also shared the opening to Schreier’s review on Bluesky and wrote, “This is honestly enough to get me to buy a PS5 and pick up this game.”

Alas, he followed this up a short time later with another Bluesky post saying, “Actually, just saw what they’re charging for these things. Never mind. I’ll play it in like 10 years.”

#3737. All GTA 6 Smartphone Apps And What They Do

Grand Theft Auto games have regularly kept up with the times, and in GTA 6, you once again have a smartphone that you can use to interact with the world around you. From getting new missions to goofing off by wasting some in-game time on social media, the smartphone in GTA 6 is a pretty handy tool for rising up the social--and criminal--ranks of Leonida. It comes equipped with several apps, and while not every one of them is essential, you'll want to keep an eye open for certain notifications. Here's a closer look at what each app does.

How to use your smartphone

As a quick reminder, you can whip out your smartphone by using the Up key on the D-pad. From there, you can navigate through the apps menu using the directional keys.

GTA 6 smartphone apps

WAiNK

The bread-and-butter app for aspiring car thieves, the WAiNK app can be used to inspect vehicles for any hidden security features. Scanning a car will let you see its estimated value, which security features it has installed, if it's locked, and how much it'll cost to register it under your name.

Scooter Bros

Need your personal vehicle in a hurry? A call to Scooter Bros will allow you to summon your ride to your location, so long as you don't mind the couriers stashing their little two-wheeled ride in your trunk.

Whatup

GTA 6's instant messaging app, this will allow you to get scoops and chat to characters, without ever needing to verbally engage with them. It's also useful for getting new missions and tips on how to make some quick cash with side-activities.

Camera

It's a camera. It can take selfies. What else were you expecting?

Gallery

Nothing too surprising here, as the Gallery app is used for checking out all the smartphone pictures you took. It also has a few archived pictures, which show off Jason and Lucia's life prior to the events that kicked off the GTA 6 storyline.

Fitness

Staying in shape is highly recommended in GTA 6, and this fitness app will allow you to track your gains and how your stats are steadily leveling up from all those deadlifting sessions.

Snapmatic

Do a little doomscrolling on the side with the social media app, which has a feed full of Leonida's citizens posting about their daily lives, as well as plenty of memes and brainrot content. You can even like posts and read the comments attached to them--if you dare.

News

Leonida is a busy city, and the news app will let you keep track of all the latest developments.

Weather

How many seasons can you expect in a single day? Check the weather app to find out.

Settings

It's not too detailed, but the option to change Jason's wallpaper and ringtone in the settings menu is a nice little touch.

While the smartphone will be a handy companion, you can also check out our GTA 6 guides hub for even more tips and tricks. It's being constantly updated with new walkthroughs and features, so if you want to check out the full list of GTA 6 radio stations, how to increase your wanted level, and much more, the answers are only a click away.

#3736. Glenn Close Gets Teary-Eyed as She Finally Gets Her Oscar at the Governors Awards

The day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” said Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

The presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

This year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he said with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

As Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she says. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”

She wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” said Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”

Many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close said she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”

#3735. Matthew McConaughey's 3 Kids Look All Grown Up on the Red Carpet

The apples don’t fall far from the tree in Matthew McConaughey’s household.

The Oscar winner and wife Camila Alves’ three children looked all grown up and every bit at home as they made a rare red carpet appearance together on Thursday, November 19, at the Los Angeles premiere of Way of the Warrior Kid.

The couple’s eldest son, Levi McConaughey, was supported by his younger siblings, sister Vida, 16, and brother Livingston, 13, at the premiere of his latest movie, which costars Chris Pratt.

The sibling trio were all smiles as they posed for photos together. Levi looked suave in a dark suit with a light blue shirt, while Livingston opted for a light blue suit with a white T-shirt. Vida looked elegant in a white dress.

Levi has been following in his famous dad’s acting footsteps in recent years. He first appeared alongside Matthew, 57, in The Lost Bus, which was released in 2025.

In a joint interview with his dad for People last year, Levi admitted he was beginning to feel the pressure of being Matthew McConaughey’s son.

“Yeah, it’s just starting,” Levi shared. “And as much as people can say, ‘Oh, you got this because of your father or your mother,’ they can open the door, but then it’s going to be up to me to do my thing once I get in there. That’s on me.”

Levi said “you got to have some chops” to make it as an actor, adding, “And so, yes, it’d feel like it would be a disservice to them because of how hard they’ve worked to get to the position that they’re at to not take advantage of it, but also put in the work and get after it and do it.”

In October 2025, Matthew said that his son earned his role in The Lost Bus on his own merit.

“I’m not putting that pressure on him either way. But he’s off to a great start, and he’s in the door,” Matthew said on Sunday Today With Willie Geist.

“As far as nepotism goes for me, Camila and I always say, ‘Don’t you ever feel entitled,’” he continued. “When he read for this role, I sent it to the casting director. She said, ‘I think it’s good enough to send to the director.’ And I went, ‘Pull his last name.’”

Matthew also opened up about the pride he felt seeing Levi on set.

“There was an extra sort of soul to it for me,” he admitted. “I said, ‘I can help coach you, I can help teach you what I can, but once we show up on the day, I’m not there as a safety net.’ And he showed up. He was not looking at me like, ‘Hey, is it OK?’ Uh-uh,” the actor said. “He worked with the director, and I sat back as a proud dad going, ‘There we go!’”

#3732. PlayStation Plus Is Losing More Games, But One Departure Stings The Most

New arrivals are landing in the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, but at the same time, you can also expect a few departures from that gaming library. Fortunately, the number of games leaving soon are on the smaller side, as there'll be only three exits in total. Unfortunately, one of those games that you're running out of time to play through the Game Catalog is a massive and pretty fun fantasy title, so get those hours in while you can.

PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon

  • Granblue Fantasy Relink
  • Somerville
  • Fade to Silence

This month's biggest departure is Granblue Fantasy Relink, a massive fantasy game with a storybook art style, cinematic boss fights, and a large roster of characters who all possess unique abilities to master. First released in February 2024, Granblue Fantasy Relink is built around real-time combat and flashy team-up mechanics, making for a visually striking experience overall. While the story isn't much to write home about, it's the gameplay and worldbuilding where this Granblue spin-off shines, and it got even better earlier this year with the Endless Ragnarok expansion.

In comparison, Somerville is a story-rich puzzle game that's oozing atmosphere with its slick art direction, and Fade to Silence is a single-player and co-op survival-crafting adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world that is feeling the chill of an eternal winter.

While the Game Catalog is going to be a little poorer without those three titles, it is getting some great games this month. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is the headline act, and it'll be joined by several more titles like Atomfall, Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake, and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii. All PlayStation Plus subscribers can also grab a trio of freebies between now and November 30: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered, and Monster Train 2.
